messages.subject: Combining 4 data sets with same names
messages.subject_clean: Combining 4 data sets with same names
messages.body_plain:
Hello
I am working with some longitudinal data, which was sent to me in four
files, called baseline, ipt, three and six.  These were originally in
SPSS (which I do not have) and I have imported them to R

Each has the same variable names (several hundred of them) ...
although one file has a few extra.  Each has more or less the same
people, but not completely.  There is an ID variable (PARTICIPANT_ID)

I would now like to make some plots of how variables changed over
time, using ggplot2.  But first, I need to somehow get the files
together.

This is my first attempt with plyr, and I am sort of floundering.

Any help appreciatted

Thanks

Peter

messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,

With only four files, you don't really need to use plyr.  I'd try
something like:

a <- read.csv("first-file.csv")
b <- read.csv("second-file.csv")
c <- read.csv("third-file.csv")
d <- read.csv("fourth-file.csv")

ab <- merge(a, b)
abc <- merge(ab, c)
abcd <- merge(abc, d)

checking each of the merges in turn to make sure that you're not
losing any data.

Hadley

messages.subject: using own function in ddply
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have the follwing df and code:

df <- data.frame(t = c(1,1,2,2,2), a = c(8,4,9,3,4), b = c(10,3,4,NA,
5), c=c(1,2,3,4,5))
df
diff <- function(df, v1, v2){
	df <- df[,c(v1,v2)]
	diff <- mean(df[,v1]-df[,v2], na.rm=T)
	diff
	}
dlply(df, .(t), transform, ab.diff = diff(x, 'a', 'b'), ac.diff = diff
(x, 'b', 'c'))

As you might imagine, that's just an example of an own function, which
does something to two or more variables within a data.frame.
Furthermore, I want to be in control of the variable names when I call
the function within ddply/dlply. diff() is much too complex for its
purpose in this example, but my original function is much more complex
and relies on the new df within the function.
Can you point me into the correct direction?

Thanks, Stefan

messages.subject: Re: using own function in ddply
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stefan,

I'd write your function like this

my_diff <- function(a, b) mean(a - b, na.rm = T)

and then call it like:

dlply(df, .(t), transform,
  ab.diff = my_diff(a, b),
  ac.diff = my_diff(b, c))

Hadley
